title: Ang 876–879: Ramkali begins
hookLine: Guru Nanak opens the calm raga
tomorrow: two more Gurus sing Ramkali. what does each one add?

cards: A friend's study setup: a ten-hour playlist, three apps, a color-coded planner, and somehow no studying yet. None of it is wrong. It just piles up, until the simpler question gets lost: what do you actually know?
On ang 876, Guru Nanak opens raga Ramkali by listing everyone's methods, and then saying what he knows instead.

teach.b: In paraphrase: some read Sanskrit, some read the Puranas; some chant the Name on prayer beads, absorbed in meditation.

teach.h: I KNOW ONLY YOUR ONE NAME.
teach.b: Then: now or ever, I know nothing; I recognize only your one Name. He doesn't mock the readers or the bead-counters. He lists them, and then sets down his own plain sentence.
Close by, Guru Nanak speaks to yogis in their own language.
In paraphrase: awareness of the Word is my horn, the singi, which the people hear; honor is my bag, and the Name is the alms I receive. A yogi's tools become pictures of the inner life.
That's Ramkali's opening calm: not a pile of methods, one Name.
Now hold this week up. The ballad, sung with the Name in the mouth. Kabir's joy, mad with praise.
Three Bhagats closing Bilaval, one with a blunt question. A sesame seed of effort, never lost.
The Guru's image, carried as the Word. And an elephant that bowed. Two ragas behind you, a third begun.

how: Ramkali is one of the Granth's ragas; its section opens on ang 876 with Guru Nanak's hymns, and later holds Anand Sahib, which Sikhs recite in daily prayer.

games.q: a friend is overwhelmed by meditation apps, books and methods, and asks where to even start. what does Ramkali's first hymn suggest?
o: start with one Name, held simply; methods can come later.
try every method in turn until one finally works.
methods are wrong; Guru Nanak rejects reading scripture.
games.why: Guru Nanak lists the methods without mocking them, then says: I recognize only your one Name.

practice: Close your eyes, rest your hands open, and set down every method for the sit: no counting, no technique. If a word comes, let it be one name you hold dear, then let it go again. If you'd like, read ang 877 first.

wordCard.voice: Ang 876. Where raga Ramkali begins, and a new stretch of the walk, with Guru Nanak's one Name.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: singi, a yogi's horn; in Ramkali Guru Nanak makes awareness of the Word his singi.

carryVoice: Ramkali: a calm raga, and one Name in place of a pile of methods. A new stretch, begun.
